subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a runtime-agnostic agent-core protocol for no-Node embedded and bare-metal ports, or keep those ports external until they identify a specific missing plugin/SDK seam?
rationale: Current code and docs still enforce a Node-hosted runtime, while VISION.md and AGENTS.md make this a core product/API boundary choice rather than an autonomous bug fix.

options.title: Keep canonical RFC
options.body: Keep this issue open for maintainer-owned protocol design covering schemas, conformance tests, platform adapters, and security boundaries before implementation PRs.

options.title: Narrow to plugin seams
options.body: Defer no-Node runtime work and pursue only smaller plugin or SDK seams such as JSON-RPC plugin bindings when they have focused implementation candidates.

options.title: Reject core sponsorship
options.body: Close the core request and ask external ports like MimiClaw to remain independent unless they uncover a specific OpenClaw API gap.

recommendation.title: Keep canonical RFC
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for maintainer-owned protocol design covering schemas, conformance tests, platform adapters, and security boundaries before implementation PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from the existing keep-open comment and the runtime/harness history behind this boundary.
